page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features the AWS Graviton family ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, delivering 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is configured at 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core). Cache hierarchy consists of 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. Cryptographic processing is accelerated via dedicated hardware AES support.

Network connectivity features a high baseline bandwidth of 33 Gbps. The instance provides no integrated local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent file systems and data persistence. Hardware acceleration via discrete GPUs is omitted, centering the resource profile purely on core compute and memory performance.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory throughput and database operation metrics. Uncached 256MB memory bandwidth achieves 294.53 GB/sec read and 132.58 GB/sec write speeds, falling into the top quartile. The PassMark memory test reaches the top tier (3216.25), while PassMark database operations also perform strongly with 24,174.88 points. Decompression tasks yield elevated throughput, recording 202.01 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3. Conversely, general compute benchmarks such as Geekbench (15,875 multi-core score) and Stress-NG (27,304.05 multi-core) register in the middle 50% band. LLM prompt processing for medium 7B models demonstrates lower comparative throughput at 31.06 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c8gb.4xlarge leverages custom ARM silicon to provide high core counts and wide memory bandwidth at a favorable resource density relative to traditional x86 alternatives. Tradeoffs include the total absence of onboard NVMe storage and lack of x86 vector instruction sets like AVX-512, which limits its utility for specialized x86 binaries. It is best suited for compute-bound microservices, multi-threaded batch compression, continuous integration build clusters, and in-memory or caching data pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gb.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor running on the AWS Nitro System. Configured with 16 dedicated physical cores (16 vCPUs) at 2.8 GHz and 32.0 GB of memory, it provides a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio. Network capacity is supported by a 33 Gbps baseline, while no local disk storage or GPU accelerators are provisioned. Benchmark evaluations place memory subsystem performance in the upper tiers, highlighted by an uncached read bandwidth of 294.53 GB/sec and strong database operation throughput. General compute tasks, Clang compilation, and static web serving deliver mid-tier results, whereas LLM prompt processing on medium models shows lower performance. The instance provides strong hardware efficiency for multi-threaded build jobs, distributed microservices, network-intensive applications, and data batch processing pipelines that do not depend on x86 instruction sets or local NVMe storage.
